items.title: Finite type descends along a surjective flat open morphism of locally ringed spaces
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a morphism of locally ringed spaces that is open on underlying spaces and surjective and flat, a sheaf of modules on the target is of finite type as soon as its pullback is (statement lines 2126-2137). The proof is a stalkwise argument carried out with explicit bookkeeping. It chooses a point of the target and a preimage, picks finitely many sections generating the pullback over an open neighbourhood of that preimage, and then uses the description of the pullback as a tensor product of the inverse image sheaf with the structure sheaf to rewrite those generators as finite sums of tensors (proof lines 2140-2146); after shrinking it may assume the inverse image sections come from sections of the original sheaf over an open set of the target, which produces a map from a finite direct sum of the structure sheaf to the original sheaf (proof lines 2147-2153). The pullback of that map is surjective by construction, and the substance of the argument is the step from surjectivity after tensoring with the stalk of the structure sheaf to surjectivity of the original stalk map, which uses that the local ring map is flat and hence faithfully flat (proof lines 2154-2164). Openness of the morphism then promotes the neighbourhood on which the generators live back to a neighbourhood of the chosen point of the target (proof lines 2165-2166). The claim is H2: the tensor rewriting is bookkeeping, but the faithfully flat descent of the surjectivity of a stalk map is the real step, and it is displayed rather than cited.
